subject: Region seal and snapshot policy Q&A – dedicated deployment confirmation
messages:
From: Alice Bennett <alice.bennett@nimbusbank.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: Chris O'Neill <chris.oneill@finwell.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 10:12:00 +0000
Subject: Questions on region pinning, snapshots and proof of deletion for dedicated cluster

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. A couple of follow-ups from our security and infra teams so we can sign off on the Dedicated deployment: 

1) Region pinning: we need a description of the technical and operational controls that guarantee tenant compute and storage remain within the EU region you pin (including metadata, snapshots, backups). Does Redwood ever replicate snapshots to another region for durability? If so, under what conditions?

2) Snapshot retention: what is the default snapshot cadence and retention for customer volumes on Dedicated? Can we request shorter retention for our tenant (we want 7 days max for ephemeral snapshots)?

3) Deletion proof: when we request a tenant wipe, what evidence does Redwood provide? We expect a list of artifacts (snapshot ids, replica locations, timestamps) and a signed attestation.

4) Logs and audit trails: are control-plane audit logs stored outside the pinned region? If yes, are they encrypted and do you support region-local logging?

Please attach any runbook snippets or manifests we can include in our internal compliance packet.

Best,
Alice Bennett
Senior Infosec Manager
NimbusBank

From: mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Alice Bennett <alice.bennett@nimbusbank.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 13:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Questions on region pinning, snapshots and proof of deletion for dedicated cluster

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together answers and attached a short checklist + a snapshot manifest example. High level: Redwood Dedicated supports tenant-level region anchoring for compute and storage; customer data paths are pinned to the chosen cloud region and we do not perform cross-region snapshot replication by default. We can, however, enable cross-region replication if a customer requests multi-region DR — this is a deliberate opt-in and would be reflected in the tenancy config.

Quick answers: 
- Region pinning: logical and physical controls — compute pinned to region-specific GPU pools; object storage configured with region-local buckets; network egress ACLs enforce regional routing. We include a post-provision verification that lists the region for compute and primary storage endpoints.
- Snapshot replication: OFF by default. Durable backup replication to other regions is only performed when the customer opts into DR. For your Dedicated cluster (NB-2026-0457) replication is currently disabled.
- Snapshot retention: default is 30 days for automatic snapshots. We can set a 7-day policy for your tenant; that requires an update to the tenant retention profile (no infra migration).
- Deletion proof: we provide a deletion manifest containing: list of deleted snapshot ids, storage object manifests, timestamps, and the ops run id. For higher assurance we will include a signed ops attestation (PGP) and a cropped log excerpt showing the deletion job execution.
- Audit logs: control-plane audit events are optionally routed to region-local syslog/S3 for customers on Dedicated. By default, aggregated control-plane logs are stored in the control plane region; we can enable region-local logging for NimbusBank.

Attachments: redwood_region_pin_checklist.pdf (runbook checklist), tenant_snapshot_manifest.csv (example), wipe-runbook-snippet.txt (ops steps & command outputs).

Next steps: I can schedule a quick session with Kimberly (engineering) to show the post-provision verification report and with Dylan to lock the retention window. Would Thursday 10–11 CET work?

Regards,
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Alice Bennett <alice.bennett@nimbusbank.com>, mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 09:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Questions on region pinning, snapshots and proof of deletion for dedicated cluster

Hi Alice — following up on Mateo's note with a couple of operational clarifications we typically include in the compliance packet: 

1) Snapshot ingestion and manifest: each snapshot has a manifest line with object hashes and primary region tag; manifests are kept in the tenant's primary bucket and included in the deletion manifest.

2) Wipe workflow: delete request -> create ephemeral verification snapshot -> delete objects -> run scrub job -> publish deletion manifest -> sign attestation -> close ticket. The ephemeral verification snapshot is never replicated.

3) For customers requiring cryptographic proof of deletion we can provide the scrub job's content-addressed receipts and a signed attestation. Note that underlying cloud provider retention windows (object versioning) are respected — we coordinate with your security team to confirm the effective erase window.

4) Evidence package content: CSV of snapshot ids & object hashes, ops run id, timestamps (UTC), list of storage endpoints (all region-tagged), and the PGP-signed attestation.

I'll be on the call with Mateo and Dylan on Thursday to walk through a sample verification report.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Dedicated Services
Redwood Inference

From: Alice Bennett <alice.bennett@nimbusbank.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Chris O'Neill <chris.oneill@finwell.com>, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 16:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Questions on region pinning, snapshots and proof of deletion for dedicated cluster

Team — thanks, that address most of our concerns. A few final asks before we move to legal sign-off: 

• Please set the snapshot retention for NB-2026-0457 to 7 days and confirm in the post-provision verification report.
• Include the PGP-signed deletion attestation template in the evidence package for review.
• Can you confirm whether control-plane metadata (tenant IDs, timestamps) are ever stored in a US region for analytics? We need explicit confirmation they stay in the EU unless we agree otherwise.

If you can deliver the verification report + attestation template by EOD Friday (Aug 14) that would let us close the security checklist. Happy to jump on the Thursday call but if you can just send the artifacts that works too.

Best,
Alice
